retiredSeed.name: Alpha Generation (AlphaGen)
retiredSeed.description: Alpha Generation is ArcLight's management platform for a large portfolio of power generation assets in the United States. The platform serves wholesale power markets through strategic management and oversight of existing thermal generation assets rather than through greenfield development alone. ArcLight stated in 2024 that AlphaGen was formed to oversee about 14 GW of power infrastructure across four U.S. competitive power markets and a portfolio generating nearly $2 billion of annual revenue. Its role is therefore operational and portfolio-oriented, covering commercial, strategic, and asset-management functions across multiple generation subsidiaries. ArcLight announced the creation of AlphaGen in January 2024 as part of the management structure for ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII, while public sources do not disclose the internal ownership split within the platform.

ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VII formed AlphaGen in January 2024 and remains the controlling majority owner. ADIA holds a separately evidenced 16.8% indirect interest through Black Volt B 2024 LLC. CPP Investments completed a US$1.0 billion strategic minority investment through CPPIB AlphaGen US LLC on March 9, 2026. Exact ArcLight and CPP ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed, and no subsequent exit or pending sale was identified through August 12, 2026.

retiredSeed.name: Cleco Corporation
retiredSeed.description: Cleco Corporation is the holding company for Cleco Group LLC, a regulated electric utility platform serving Louisiana through Cleco Power and related generation assets. Cleco serves approximately 298,000 residential, commercial, and industrial customers in 24 Louisiana parishes, owns eight generating units with 2,676 MW of rated capacity, and remains regulated by the Louisiana Public Service Commission. The business is asset-heavy and largely regulated, with earnings supported by utility networks, generation assets, and approved tariffs. A North American investor group led by Macquarie Infrastructure and Real Assets and BCI completed the take-private acquisition in April 2016. On April 27, 2026, Stonepeak and Bernhard Capital Partners announced an agreement to acquire Cleco from Macquarie Asset Management, BCI, and Manulife Investment Management, but the transaction remained subject to customary regulatory approvals as of May 12, 2026, so the BCI holding remains active until a closing is confirmed.

retiredSeed.name: Puget Energy / Puget Sound Energy
retiredSeed.description: Puget Energy is the holding company for Puget Sound Energy, Washington's regulated electric and gas utility. The utility serves approximately 1.2 million electric customers and 900,000 natural gas customers across a 6,000-square-mile service territory in 10 counties. Its operating model is asset-heavy and regulated, with revenue supported by utility rate structures, generation assets, transmission, distribution, and long-lived network infrastructure. AIMCo has held the investment since the 2009 take-private and increased its stake in 2018, while the current public consortium also includes Macquarie, Ontario Teachers', OMERS, BCI, and PGGM. BCI's 2024 I&RR financial statements disclose a 20.9% ownership interest in Puget Sound Energy, and BCI continued to describe PSE as one of its largest and longest-standing infrastructure investments in 2025.

retiredSeed.name: U.S. Medical Outpatient Facilities Portfolio (MedCraft JV)
retiredSeed.description: U.S. Medical Outpatient Facilities Portfolio (MedCraft JV) is a portfolio of medical outpatient buildings in the United States. Its end users are patients and healthcare providers, with occupancy tied to a major nonprofit health system under a sale-leaseback structure rather than broad multi-tenant speculative leasing. The model is asset-heavy and healthcare-oriented, with value supported by essential outpatient real estate and a large health-system tenant. Fengate disclosed in 2025 that the portfolio comprises 24 facilities with more than 900,000 square feet of medical space across two states. The reviewed materials did not disclose the specific states, property-level revenue, or current ownership percentages within the joint venture. Fengate acquired the portfolio in 2025 alongside MedCraft as part of its healthcare infrastructure strategy.
